events.description: United States killed Ayman al-Zawahiri; his deputy Saif al-Adel, based in Iran, became al-Qaeda leader
'Twelve-day war' in June (Iran conflict); Saif al-Adel did not leave Iran during or after it
Saif al-Adel reportedly travelled to Afghanistan at least once after the fall of the Afghan government and Zawahiri's death to handle al-Qaeda leadership consolidation (trips, not residence)

UN 1267 Monitoring Team report (written by end of December 2025) says al-Qaeda leadership 'cohesive, though isolated', rank-and-file dissatisfied with Saif al-Adel, AQ retains ambition for spectacular external attacks; omits Saif's location for the third consecutive report
actors: UN Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team

events.description: Khalid Batarfi (previous AQAP leader) and Saif al-Adel's son died in Yemen within a month of each other (natural causes / domestic accident); unexplained per hosts
UN report references a possible strategic meeting between the Houthis, AQAP and al-Shabaab
ISIS attack on Jewish revelers at Bondi Beach, Sydney; assailants had spent time in southern Philippines before the attack
ISIS attack in Kerman, Iran, and Crocus concert hall attack in Moscow cited as ISIS attacks on Iran and Russia
JNIM instituted a fuel blockade around Bamako and expanded territory; a single ransom payment of around $50 million reported
Hurras al-Din announced it was disbanding after Sharaa took control of Syria (late Jan / early Feb 2025) while saying it would 'stand by for further developments'
Sharaa met and shook hands with the US president; US sanctions removed from HTS and from Sharaa personally
Syrian government attacked the SDF in mid-to-late January 2026, raising fears for the ISIS camps and prisons
Three Americans, including two soldiers, killed in Syria; US subsequently targeted the Islamic State (host notes the perpetrator was reportedly linked to Hurras al-Din)
Abu Khadija, head of the Islamic State's General Directorate of Provinces, killed
President Trump launched strikes in Nigeria against people accused of killing Christians
ISIS Mozambique captured Mocimboa da Praia, a port in Cabo Delgado ('a couple of years ago')
SIGAR disbanded 'within the last several weeks'
actors: Special Inspector General for Afghanistan Reconstruction

events.description: Israel recognised Somaliland as independent from Somalia, upsetting Turkey, Saudi Arabia and others
Cabrera v. Islamic Republic of Iran: Roggio was a lead witness; case showed Iran provided weapons, training, safe haven and intelligence to the Taliban and al-Qaeda ('the syndicate')

key_claims: Al-Qaeda's emir Saif al-Adel is in Iran as a guest of the Iranian government and has not left, including through the June 2025 war; the UN report's silence on his location is its biggest weakness.
Since Zawahiri's death on 31 Jul 2022, Iran effectively controls al-Qaeda, which is becoming at least a partial member of Iran's axis of resistance.
Saif al-Adel made at least one trip to Afghanistan after the fall of Kabul to consolidate al-Qaeda leadership, using safe houses along the Afghan-Iranian border, but he resides in Iran.

AQAP under Saad al-Awlaki is asserting more global leadership and is now allied with the Houthis; a possible Houthi-AQAP-al-Shabaab strategic meeting reflects Saif al-Adel's Iran relationship, not a split.
The unexplained deaths of Khalid Batarfi and Saif al-Adel's son within a month of each other in Yemen remain a leadership puzzle.
Al-Qaeda, not ISIS, is the greater long-term strategic threat: JNIM blockades Bamako and expands into Nigeria with Ansaru; the Taliban host al-Qaeda camps; Sharaa's Syria is al-Qaeda-influenced.
ISIS's two top posts may both be held by Africans (Mumin in Somalia and al-Mainuki in Nigeria), but the hosts doubt the Arab-chauvinist organization would accept an African caliph.
Hurras al-Din's 2025 'disbandment' is nominal; its cells remain in southern Syria with allegiance to al-Qaeda.
Mullah Omar's death was concealed by the Taliban, a precedent for al-Qaeda concealing Zawahiri's death and its new emir.
